name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Security Deposit Refund Dispute – 2BHK HSR Layout
case_dossier.summary: The tenant vacated a 2BHK flat after a 2‑year lease, handed over the property in good condition, and was promised a full security deposit refund. The landlord now claims a Rs 45,000 deduction for repainting and cleaning, which the tenant disputes.

timeline.event: Tenancy of 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru began at Rs 28,000/month with Rs 1,00,000 security deposit.
Tenant gave one‑month notice to vacate.
Tenant vacated the flat, cleared electricity and water bills, handed over keys, and recorded move‑out video.
Landlord promised to refund the full deposit via UPI within three days.
No refund received; landlord stopped answering calls.
Landlord messaged tenant stating a deduction of Rs 45,000 for repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: Move‑out handover video showing condition of the property
Bank statements showing monthly rent payments
WhatsApp chat where landlord acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition
UPI transaction history (showing no refund received)
evidence_needed: Signed rent agreement/lease deed specifying security deposit terms and permissible deductions
Receipt or written acknowledgment of the Rs 1,00,000 security deposit paid
Copy of the one‑month notice sent on 1 Oct 2024
Utility bill clearance receipts (electricity, water) for October 2024
Any written estimate or invoice from landlord for repainting/marble polishing/cleaning
Inventory or condition checklist (if any) signed by both parties at move‑in and move‑out
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong visual and transactional proof of the flat's condition and payments, plus landlord's acknowledgment, but missing the formal lease and written notice documents which are crucial for a complete case.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You, as the tenant, have a solid legal footing to claim the full return of your security deposit. Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only liable for damage that goes beyond normal wear and tear (Section 108(B)(m)). The photographs and video you have taken show that the flat was handed back in good condition, and the landlord’s own WhatsApp message confirms this. Because the landlord has not provided any written estimate or invoice proving that the Rs 45,000 deduction is for actual damage, the deduction is not legally justified. 

Since the dispute is about a contract‑based monetary claim, it is a civil matter, not a criminal one. You can recover the amount through a simple pre‑litigation notice and, if needed, by approaching the Rent Authority or a Small Causes Court in Bengaluru. The process is straightforward, inexpensive, and you can represent yourself without hiring a lawyer.

governing_laws.relevance: Limits the landlord’s right to deduct from the deposit to damages beyond reasonable wear and tear. Your evidence shows only normal wear, so the deduction is unlawful.
Allows a tenant to make necessary repairs and deduct the cost only after giving the landlord a reasonable notice and receiving a written estimate. No such notice or estimate was given.
Guarantees the tenant’s right to quiet enjoyment and possession without arbitrary deductions, reinforcing your claim for a full refund.

action_options.title: Send a Formal Legal Notice to the Landlord
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (Speed Post or email)
action_options.details: Draft a notice citing Section 108(B)(m) and Section 108(B)(f) of the Transfer of Property Act. State that the deposit must be returned in full because no proven damage beyond reasonable wear and tear exists. Attach copies of the move‑out video, photographs, rent payment statements, and the landlord’s WhatsApp acknowledgment. Demand payment of the full Rs 1,00,000 deposit within 15 days, failing which you will proceed to legal action.

action_options.title: File a Complaint with the Local Rent Authority / Small Causes Court
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees up to Rs. 5 Lakhs (Small Causes Court) + nominal filing fee
action_options.details: If the landlord does not comply, lodge an application before the Bengaluru Rent Authority (under Karnataka’s Rent Control Act) or file a suit for recovery of deposit in the Small Causes Court of Bangalore. Prepare the same documents used in the notice, plus a copy of the lease (if available) and the one‑month notice you sent. The court can order the landlord to refund the deposit with interest and may award costs.

action_options.title: Approach the Consumer Forum (Optional)
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal (court fee based on claim value)
action_options.details: If the landlord continues to refuse payment, you may also file a complaint under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 for unfair trade practice (Section 2(47)). Use the e‑Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) to submit the complaint with all evidence. The Consumer Commission can order a refund and may impose a penalty on the landlord.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can draft and send the legal notice yourself, and you are allowed to appear personally before the Rent Authority, Small Causes Court, or Consumer Forum. A lawyer becomes essential only if the case becomes complex (e.g., multiple parties, counter‑claims) or if you wish to file an appeal. For the steps outlined above, self‑representation is fully permissible.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

## **LEGAL NOTICE**  
*(Demand for Refund of Security Deposit – 2BHK HSR Layout, Bengaluru)*  

---

### **Date:** 07‑11‑2026  

### **Mode of Dispatch:**  
- **Speed Post – Acknowledgement Due (AD)**  *(or)*  
- **Registered Email (with read‑receipt)**  

---

### **From (Sender / Claimant)**  

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **Name:** | **[Your Full Name]** |
| **Address:** | **[Flat No., Street, HSR Layout, Bengaluru – 560102]** |
| **Phone:** | **[Mobile No.]** |
| **E‑mail:** | **[your.email@example.com]** |

### **To (Recipient / Opposite Party)**  

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **Name:** | **Mr. Ramesh** |
| **Address:** | **[Landlord’s Complete Postal Address]** |
| **Phone / Email:** | **[If known]** |

## **Subject:**  
**Demand for Full Refund of Security Deposit (Rs. 1,00,000) within 15 Days of Receipt of this Notice**  

---

### **1.  Under instructions from my client, the undersigned hereby submits as under:**  

| Sr. No. | Date / Period | Event |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Oct 2022 (approx.)** | Tenancy of the 2 BHK flat (HSR Layout, Bengaluru) commenced on a month‑to‑month basis at **Rs 28,000 per month**. A **security deposit of Rs 1,00,000** was paid by the tenant to the landlord. |
| 2 | **1 Oct 2024** | Tenant served a **one‑month notice** to vacate the premises, as required under the lease. |
| 3 | **31 Oct 2024** | Tenant vacated the flat, cleared all electricity & water dues, handed over the keys, and recorded a **move‑out video** showing the flat in good condition. |
| 4 | **Early Nov 2024 (within 3 days of vacating)** | Landlord **promised** to refund the **full security deposit** via UPI **within three days**. |
| 5 | **~25 Nov 2024 (25 days after vacating)** | No refund was received; landlord stopped answering calls. |
| 6 | **26 Nov 2024** | Landlord messaged the tenant stating a **deduction of Rs 45,000** for repainting, marble polishing and deep cleaning. No written estimate, invoice or inspection report was furnished. |

---

### **2.  Documents/ Evidence in the possession of the tenant (Annexure‑A)**  

1. Move‑in photographs of the flat.  
2. Move‑out hand‑over video (showing condition of the property).  
3. Bank statements evidencing monthly rent payments.  
4. WhatsApp chat screenshot where landlord **acknowledged receipt of the flat in good condition**.  
5. UPI transaction history (showing **no refund** received).  

*(All the above are annexed hereto and form part of this notice.)*  

---

### **3.  Legal Grounds**  

| Provision | Act | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| **Section 108(B)(m)** | Transfer of Property Act, 1882 | Allows deduction from security deposit **only for damage beyond normal wear and tear**. The tenant’s video & photographs demonstrate only ordinary wear; therefore the claimed Rs 45,000 is unlawful. |
| **Section 108(B)(f)** | Transfer of Property Act, 1882 | Requires the landlord to give **reasonable notice** and a **written estimate/invoice** for any deduction. No such notice or estimate has been provided. |
| **Section 108(A)(c)** | Transfer of Property Act, 1882 | Guarantees the tenant’s right to **quiet enjoyment and possession** without arbitrary deductions. |

---

### **4.  Demand**  

In view of the foregoing facts and legal provisions, the tenant **demands** that the landlord:

1. **Refund the entire security deposit of Rs 1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh only)** **without any deduction**,  
2. **Within fifteen (15) days** from the date of receipt of this notice (i.e., by **22‑11‑2026**),  
3. Payment to be made by **UPI/Bank Transfer** to the following account:  
   - **Account Holder:** *[Your Name]*  
   - **Bank & IFSC:** *[Bank Details]*  
   - **UPI ID:** *[your.upi@bank]*  

**Failure to comply** with the above demand within the stipulated period will attract the following consequences **without any further notice**:

| Consequence | Legal Basis | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Interest** | [unverified reference removed] of the **Rural Debt Recovery Act, 1999** (as applied by courts) | Statutory interest at **12 % per annum** from the date of default (27 Nov 2024) until actual payment. |
| **Litigation Costs & Damages** | Civil Procedure Code, 1908 – Order II Rule 9 | Recovery of all court fees, attorney’s fees (if any), and **liquidated damages** for breach of contract. |
| **Legal Action** | Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1999 & Small Causes Court (Bengaluru) | Filing of a suit for recovery of the deposit with interest and costs before the **Bengaluru Rent Authority** or **Small Causes Court**. |
| **Consumer Protection** | Consumer Protection Act, 2019 – Section 2(47) (Unfair Trade Practice) | Parallel complaint before the **Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** (District/State) for unfair deduction. |

---

### **5.  Annexure‑A (List of Documents attached)**  

| No. | Document |
|---|---|
| 1 | Move‑in photographs (dated Oct 2022) |
| 2 | Move‑out hand‑over video (31 Oct 2024) |
| 3 | Bank statements showing rent payments (Oct 2022 – Oct 2024) |
| 4 | WhatsApp chat screenshot (landlord’s acknowledgment) |
| 5 | UPI transaction history (no credit of Rs 1,00,000) |
| 6 | Copy of the one‑month notice dated 1 Oct 2024 (if available) |
| 7 | Utility bill clearance receipts (Electricity & Water – Oct 2024) |
| 8 | Any other relevant communication (e.g., landlord’s message of 26 Nov 2024) |

*(If any of the above documents are not in possession, the tenant shall procure them promptly and submit as part of the final pleading.)*  

---

### **6.  Verification**  

I, **[Your Full Name]**, the undersigned, do hereby **verify** that the contents of this notice are true to my knowledge and belief, and that no material fact has been concealed.

---  

**Signature of the Tenant**  

_____________________________  
**[Your Full Name]**  

**Date:** 07‑11‑2026

1. **Self (for records)**  
2. **District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) – Bengaluru** (for legal aid reference)  
3. **E‑mail attachment (if sent by registered email)**

> **Important:** Retain the **Speed‑Post receipt with Acknowledgement Due (AD)** as proof of service. In case the landlord disputes receipt, the AD receipt will be admissible evidence before any forum.

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, aapka video aur chat humne dekha hai, lekin hamari company policy ke mutabik agar paint ki halat normal wear‑and‑tear se zyada kharab ho to uska kharcha deposit se liya ja sakta hai. Aapne Section 108 ka zikr kiya, lekin usmein bhi yeh likha hai ki ‘actual damage’ ke liye hi deduction ho sakta hai, na ki sirf purane hone ke liye. Isliye hum aapse ek formal notice maang rahe hain – aapke saboot aur hamare inspection report ko dekh kar hi hum final decision lenge. Agar aapko lagta hai ki hum galat hain, to aap consumer court ya Karnataka Rent Control Tribunal mein appeal kar sakte hain, lekin iske liye humein aapka written notice chahiye. Tab hum 7 din ke andar aapko final settlement amount batayenge.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: Aapne sahi tarah se Section 108 aur Model Tenancy framework ka hawala diya, saath hi video aur chat proof ka zikr karke apni baat ko mazboot banaya.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Karnataka Rent Control Act ya Karnataka Rent Restriction Act ke specific clause (jaise ki [unverified reference removed] – deposit refund within 30 din) ka bhi zikr kar sakte the, aur actual repair estimate ya invoice attach karne se aapka case aur bhi pakka hota.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Agar aapko 7 din mein refund nahi milta, to main Karnataka Rent Control Tribunal mein complaint file karunga aur aapke saboot ke saath consumer court ka bhi sahara lunga.
